newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Belgrade to reopen talks with commercial creditors.
newsitem.headline: Belgrade to reopen talks with commercial creditors.

text.p: Yugoslavia will resume talks with its commercial bank creditors next Monday in London after a break of more than six months, Yugoslav Deputy Prime Minister Danko Djunic said on Wednesday.
"We go to London with concrete proposals and transparent and clear explanation(s)..." Djunic told Reuters, but declined to give details.
He said the amount Yugoslavia owes would be among the subjects of the proposals.

According to estimates by the London Club of commercial bank creditors, Serbia and Montenegro inherited $2 billion in commercial debt after the violent break-up of the former Balkan federation in 1991.
Representatives from the Yugoslav federal government, the National Bank of Yugoslavia and independent experts, will attend the talks, due to start at 13.00 local time on June 23.
The team will be led by Djunic, who is in charge of overall economic reforms, and will also include Nebojsa Maljkovic, Yugoslavia's IMF minister.
"We are ready to talk directly, very professionally and hope the other side will also be ready to talk," Djunic said.

Technical talks on a possible restructuring or rescheduling of Yugoslavia's London Club debt were last held late in 1996, when sources close to the negotiating team said the talks stumbled over Belgrade presenting an overly optimistic report on the country's economic situation.
Other major issues include how Belgrade plans to share former Yugoslavia's assets with the other successor republics and the issue of its IMF membership.
An agreement with the London Club is crucial if Belgrade is to be able to tap the international markets for funds needed to breathe life into its moribund economy.

It has frequently said it is willing to repay its foreign creditors but that it needs the cooperation of members of the international banking community in order to service its debt. -- Gordana Filipovic, Belgrade newsroom, +381 11 222 4254
